summary: Klamath County tower near Rocky Point with a 1986 metal cab built alongside a cable-company relay; standing, on standby and used only in emergencies.

facts.design: 10x10-ft metal cab on a 20-ft metal tower (1986 structure)
facts.status_note: On standby; the 1986 tower is used only during emergencies (NHLR; firelookout.com). Listed as unmanned on a standing-lookouts list.

access.note: Summit shares use with a communications relay. The cab is on standby and used only in emergencies. Cheryl Hill's list marks the site publicly accessible, which does not mean access to the lookout. No source gives visitor rules; this level is an inference.

visit.trail_note: A 1967 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description gives a rough, bladed road to the tower. No current road status found.

events.note: A 15-foot steel tower was erected for panorama photos; a lookout station was under construction in July 1934 (Oregon Lookouts quoting 1934 newspapers).
First structure, a 20-ft cable-braced pole L-4 tower, per firelookout.com. Date conflicts with the 1934 newspaper items.
Lookout reported feeling an earth tremor, per Medford Mail Tribune item quoted by Oregon Lookouts.
Newspaper notice offered the lookout post to a man and wife with a car.
A married couple was to man the 14x14-ft fire detection and communication station after snow was cleared.
Lookout shoveled through four-foot drifts; the road was reopened mid-August 1952.
A 20-ft treated timber tower with an L-4 cab replaced the first structure.
Live-in R-6 cab on a 20-ft treated timber tower. NHLR says it came twelve years after 1954; firelookout.com says 1965.
Pacific Northwest Bell unit removed in fall 1971; a later memo says it would not be reinstalled.
Newspaper describes a combined tower and communications building built by private enterprise on leased Forest Service land, with a seasonal lookout planned.
Present metal cab on a 20-ft metal tower, offered by a cable company that wanted a relay station; replaced the R-6 cab.

corrections.proposed: 10x10-ft metal cab on a 20-ft metal tower (1986 structure); the R-6 live-in cab was its predecessor, replaced in 1986
corrections.why: The R-6 cab on a 20-ft timber tower stood here from the mid-1960s until 1986; the standing structure is the 1986 metal cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR puts the R-6 cab twelve years after 1954 (about 1966); firelookout.com says 1965. The story uses 'more than a decade later' without choosing a year.
NHLR and firelookout.com both describe a 20-ft tower, which matches the record's 6.1 m. The 39-foot steel tower on the Oregon Lookouts page is not used.

notes_for_editor: Current status (standby, used only in emergencies, unmanned) rests on NHLR, firelookout.com and an undated standing-lookouts list; no Forest Service document was found and the present road and visitor status is unverified. The first-structure date conflicts: 1934 newspapers (tower erected, station under construction) versus firelookout.com's 1935. The 1980 newspaper item and the 1986 date for the present cab do not line up cleanly; the 1980 item describes a 39-foot tower and a lookout to be stationed the next summer. Elevation: register 7,994 ft (2,437 m) matches the record; firelookout.com and the standing-lookouts list give 8,035 ft. Staffing 'unstaffed' as_of 'undated' is from the standing-lookouts list and standby status. Access 'restricted' is an inference, not an official policy. One websearch (unproductive) and five page reads were used for this tower.
